A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heat stress is not a function of the ambient environment alone, but rather the combination of the ambient environment and the clothing combination worn by the worker.

heat stress indices, including core temperature and heat stress indices, increased similarly under different combinations of ambient conditions and clothing combinations, suggesting that the current TLV guidelines may be adequate for intermittent work under the environmental conditions and clothing used in this study.
core temperature, PSI, and PeSI are all good indicators of heat strain during intermittent work, and that core temperature is the best predictor of heat strain during the intermittent work period.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the WBGT is a useful tool for predicting the physiological strain in the heat for intermittent work, but it should be used in conjunction with other heat stress indices such as core and skin temperatures, and heat strain indices to provide a comprehensive assessment of the physiological strain in workers.
heat strain indices (e.g. PSI and PeSI) are not reliable indicators of heat strain during intermittent work under various combinations of effective WBGT and clothing adjustment factor conditions.
core temperature is a more sensitive indicator of heat stress than heat strain indices during intermittent work.
